description: A colleague proposes a sliding-window solution for finding the shortest subarray with sum at least K, but the array may contain negative numbers. Evaluate the proposal and describe a correct approach.
solution: The proposal is incorrect: the sliding-window shrink step relies on the sum only decreasing when an element is removed, which fails with negative numbers, because removing a negative element increases the sum and a window that currently fails could succeed after growing further. A correct approach uses prefix sums with a map from prefix value to earliest index, or, for the general case with arbitrary values, a monotonic deque over prefix sums (the standard solution for shortest subarray with sum at least K). State the assumption explicitly: sliding window for sum constraints requires non-negative numbers.
title: Sliding window with negative numbers

description: You need a leaderboard supporting frequent score updates, lookups of a player's score, and listing the top 10 players. Which structures would you combine, and what are the complexities?
solution: Use a HashMap from player to score for O(1) average lookup and update, combined with a structure for ranking. For top 10 only, a min-heap of size 10 rebuilt or maintained on updates gives O(log 10), effectively constant, per update in the simple rebuild approach, or maintain a TreeMap from score to players for O(log n) updates and O(10) top-10 reads. Avoid re-sorting all players on every update, which is O(n log n) per update, and avoid a plain list scan for lookups, which is O(n).
title: Choosing a structure for a leaderboard
